[[File:Fidel castro angel 1954.jpg|thumb|Fidelito with his imprisoned father, 1954]]
'''Fidel Ángel Castro Díaz-Balart''' (1 September 1949 – 1 February 2018) was a Cuban [[nuclear physics|nuclear physicist]] and government official. 
Frequently known by the [[diminutive]] 
'''Fidelito''' ('Little Fidel'),<ref name="History">{{cite web|url=http://www.thecubanhistory.com/2017/11/fidel-castro-diaz-balart-fidelito-history-of-fidel-castro-ruz-first-born-son-fidel-castro-diaz-balart-fidelito-historia-del-primogenito-de-fidel-castro-ruz/|title=FIDEL CASTRO Díaz-Balart, "FIDELITO". History of Fidel Castro Ruz first-born son|publisher=The Cuban History|date=27 November 2017}}</ref> he was the eldest son of Cuban leader [[Fidel Castro]] and his first wife, [[Mirta Diaz-Balart|Mirta Díaz-Balart]].<ref>{{cite news|url= http://www.newsweek.com/fidel-castro-diaz-balart-cuba-suicide-fidelito-fidel-castro-797917|title=Who Is Fidel Castro Diaz-Balart? Oldest Son of Deceased Leader Fidel Castro Committed Suicide|date= 1 February 2018|newspaper=[[Newsweek]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://heavy.com/news/2016/11/fidel-castro-children-kids-photos-daughters-sons-angel-fidelito-antonio-alejandro-alexis-alex-alina-jorge-francisca-pupo-pictures-funeral-how-many/|title=Fidel Castro's Children: The Family He Left Behind|last=Dwilson|first=Stephanie Dube|date=26 November 2016|work=[[Heavy.com]]|access-date=2 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.abendblatt.de/hamburg/article206744689/Hamburgs-Wirtschaftssenator-zu-Besuch-bei-Fidel-Castros-Sohn.html|url-access=subscription|title=Hamburgs Wirtschaftssenator zu Besuch bei Fidel Castros Sohn|last=Geisler|first=Bob|newspaper=[[Hamburger Abendblatt]]|access-date=2 February 2018|language=de}}</ref>

==Life and career==
[[File:Fidel Castro Díaz-Balart with Enrique Peña Nieto.jpg|thumb|Castro Díaz-Balart (left) with [[President of Mexico]] [[Enrique Peña Nieto]], 28 January 2014, 2nd [[Community of Latin American and Caribbean States|CELAC]] Summit, Havana.]] 
Castro Díaz-Balart's parents divorced in 1955, prior to the [[Cuban Revolution]] in which his father seized power in the country. 
His mother moved to [[Miami]], United States, with the [[Diaz-Balart|Díaz-Balart]] family, taking her son with her. Castro Díaz-Balart returned to Cuba as a child to visit his father, and remained there for the rest of his childhood.<ref name="bbc.com">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-42913492|title=Cuba: Fidel Castro's son 'takes own life'|date=1 February 2018|newspaper=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> In 1959, he appeared as a 9-year-old during an interview with his father on U.S. television.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=en5RenIJHDo |title=Fidel Castro 1959 (starting at 2:00)|work=Youtube |date=1959 |access-date=2 February 2018}}</ref>

Castro Díaz-Balart moved to [[Moscow]] (in what was then the [[Soviet Union]]), where he enrolled at [[Voronezh State University]] in 1968.<ref name="Moscow Times 2014">{{cite news|url=https://themoscowtimes.com/news/visiting-russia-fidel-castros-son-scoffs-at-us-sanctions-over-crimea-33481|title=Visiting Russia, Fidel Castro's Son Scoffs at U.S. Sanctions Over Crimea|newspaper=[[The Moscow Times]]|date=1 April 2014}}</ref> For safety, he studied under the code name "José Raúl Fernández",<ref name="tagesspiegel">{{cite web|url=http://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/kuba-fidelito-ist-tot/20919834.html |title="Fidelito" ist tot | publisher=[[Deutsche Presse-Agentur|DPA]]-Article in [[Der Tagesspiegel]] | date= 2 February 2018}}</ref> which he claimed to have chosen in homage to world chess champion [[José Raúl Capablanca]] and to have later used to publish 30 scientific publications.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/fidel-castro-s-eldest-son-physicist-victim-apparent-suicide|title=Fidel Castro's eldest son, a physicist, is victim of apparent suicide |first=Richard|last=Stone|journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|date=2 February 2018|doi=10.1126/science.aat2018 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>
He initially studied [[physical education]] before switching to [[nuclear physics]] in 1970.<ref name="Moscow Times 2014"/> He graduated from [[Lomonosov Moscow State University]], and went on to work at the [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] in [[Dubna]], and to receive his first doctorate from Lomonosov, in 1978.<ref name="Pagliery">{{cite web|url=https://www.havanatimes.org/?p=110319|title=Fidel Jr. Back in the News|first=Felipe|last=Pagliery|publisher=[[Havana Times]]|date=30 March 2015}}</ref><ref name="Moscow Times 2014"/><ref name="History"/> Returning to Cuba, he was placed in charge of Cuba's nuclear power program for a time, leading the [[Juragua Nuclear Power Plant]] construction program from 1980 to 1992, during which time he was also the executive secretary of the country's [[Atomic Energy Commission (Cuba)|Atomic Energy Commission]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bbc.com/mundo/noticias-america-latina-42827688 |title=Se suicida Fidel Castro Díaz-Balart, hijo mayor del expresidente de Cuba |date=2 February 2018|newspaper=[[BBC Mundo]]}}</ref> He served as a member of the [[Non-Aligned Movement|Non-aligned Movement]]'s Coordinating Countries for the Peaceful Use of Nuclear Energy, and was elected to chair the Second Meeting of that group in April 1983.<ref>Executive Office of the President, ''Latin America Report'' (1983), Issue 2696, p. 2.</ref> Castro Díaz-Balart was removed from his positions in June 1992, following a falling out with his father, who cited "inefficiency" as the reason for the removal.<ref name="French">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1992/09/07/world/cuba-cancels-atom-plant-blaming-costs-and-russians.html|title=Cuba Cancels Atom Plant, Blaming Costs and Russians|date=7 September 1992|first=Howard W.|last=French|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Another reason for his removal is attributed to his failure to develop an atomic bomb for Cuba's military.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Barron |first=John |date=March 1990 |title=Castro, Cocaine and the A-Bomb |journal=Reader's Digest |issue=March, 1990 |pages=65-71}}</ref> Castro then announced the suspension of construction at Juragua in September 1992, due to Cuba's inability to meet the financial terms set by Russia to complete the reactors.<ref name="French"/>

Castro Díaz-Balart then returned to further his studies in Moscow, and received his second doctorate at the [[Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy]] in 1999.<ref name="Moscow Times 2014"/> In the 2010s, he returned to a level of prominence, serving as a scientific advisor to the [[Council of State (Cuba)|Council of State]], the governing body of Cuba, and as vice-president of the [[Cuban Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of Cuba]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.granma.cu/cuba/2018-02-01/fallecio-el-companero-fidel-castro-diazbalart-01-02-2018-16-02-40 |title=Falleció el compañero Fidel Castro Díaz–Balart  |work=[[Granma (newspaper)|Granma]] |date=1 February 2018}}</ref><ref name="Reuters-S">{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cuba-castro-suicide/fidel-castros-eldest-son-fidelito-commits-suicide-idUSKBN1FM06J |title=Fidel Castro's eldest son 'Fidelito' commits suicide |work=[[Reuters]] |date=1 February 2018}}</ref> Throughout his career, Castro Diaz-Balart authored articles on the developing role of nuclear energy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.theshillongtimes.com/2018/02/02/fidel-castros-eldest-son-commits-suicide/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202135409/http://www.theshillongtimes.com/2018/02/02/fidel-castros-eldest-son-commits-suicide/|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 February 2018|title=Fidel Castro's Eldest Son Commits Suicide|work=[[Shillong Times]]|date=2 February 2018}}</ref>

In 2012, Castro Díaz-Balart disputed reports that Fidel Castro was becoming senile, describing his father as "lucid" and "working hard",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/fidel-castro-is-not-senile-still-working-hard-his-son-says-6543293|title=Fidel Castro Is Not Senile, Still "Working Hard," His Son Says|first=Tim|last=Elfrink|work=[[Miami New Times]]|date=20 September 2012}}</ref> which was similar to the "upbeat assessment" of Castro's health that Castro Díaz-Balart made in February 2007, following Castro's illness during that period.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/6367257.stm|title=Cuba's Castro recovering says son|first=Stephen|last=Gibbs|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=16 February 2007}}</ref>

In April 2014, he visited Russia to declare Cuba's recognition of the [[annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation]], also receiving an honorary doctorate at Voronezh State University.<ref name="Moscow Times 2014"/> In February 2015, during the [[Cuban thaw]] towards the end of the [[Presidency of Barack Obama|Obama administration]], when Americans were more freely allowed to visit Cuba, he participated in events to welcome American celebrities to the island, mingling with [[Paris Hilton]] and [[Naomi Campbell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/centralamericaandthecaribbean/cuba/11443590/Cubas-revolution-comes-full-circle-with-a-Hilton-in-Havana.html|title=Cuba's revolution comes full circle with a Hilton in Havana|first=Nick|last=Allen|work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]|date=1 March 2015}}</ref> The following month, he visited [[Novosibirsk]], Russia, meeting with the mayor, [[Anatoly Lokot]], and regional governor [[Vladimir Gorodetsky]] to improve Cuban relations with scientific institutions in the region.<ref name="Pagliery"/>

==Family==
{{See also|Díaz-Balart family}}
Castro Díaz-Balart had three children – Mirta María, Fidel Antonio, and José Raúl – with Natasha Smirnova, whom he met in Russia. After divorcing Smirnova, he married María Victoria Barreiro from Cuba.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.miamiherald.com/news/nation-world/world/americas/cuba/article197970074.html|title=Fidel Castro's oldest son commits suicide after battle with depression|work=[[Miami Herald]]|first1=Monique O.|last1=Madan|first2=Joey|last2=Flechas|date=2 February 2018}}</ref> U.S. Congressman [[Mario Díaz-Balart]], who represents the 25th district of Florida, and former U.S. Congressman [[Lincoln Díaz-Balart]] were his maternal cousins.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-cuba-castro-suicide/fidel-castros-eldest-son-fidelito-commits-suicide-idUKKBN1FM075 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202033120/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-cuba-castro-suicide/fidel-castros-eldest-son-fidelito-commits-suicide-idUKKBN1FM075 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 February 2018 |title=Fidel Castro's eldest son 'Fidelito' commits suicide |last1=Marsh |first1=Sarah|last2=Frank |first2=Marc |date=2 February 2018|editor-last=Maler |editor-first=Sandra|editor2-last=McCool |editor2-first=Grant|editor3-last=Cameron-Moore |editor3-first=Simon |website=[[reuters.com]]|access-date=18 March 2018}}</ref>

==Death==
Castro Díaz-Balart died by [[suicide]] in Havana on 1 February 2018, at the age of 68.<ref name="bbc.com"/> He had previously received outpatient care for [[Major depressive disorder|depression]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2018/02/01/americas/fidel-castro-son-dead/index.html|title=Fidel Castro's eldest son takes own life, state media reports|last=Oppmann|first=Patrick|date=1 February 2019|work=[[CNN]]|access-date=2 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/feb/02/fidel-castros-eldest-son-takes-his-own-life|title=Fidel Castro's eldest son dies aged 68 – reports|date=2 February 2018|website=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=2 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/fidelito-dead-dies-died-fidel-castro-diaz-balart-suicide-68-cuba-a8190391.html|title=Fidel Castro's eldest son has died|last=White|first=Jeremy|date=2 February 2018|work=[[The Independent]]|access-date=2 February 2018}}</ref> The report of his [[suicide]] by the Cuban government was described as "unusually public."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/fidel-castros-son-mourned-cuba-suicide-52800674|title=Fidel Castro's son mourned in Cuba after suicide|first=Andrea|last=Rodriguez|work=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|date=2 February 2018|access-date=3 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205030425/https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/fidel-castros-son-mourned-cuba-suicide-52800674|archive-date=5 February 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> Fidel Ángel Castro Díaz-Balart's first cousin Gabriel Díaz-Balart also died by suicide as a result of depression. "Fidelito" Castro Díaz-Balart was buried in the [[Colon Cemetery, Havana|Central Colon Cemetery]] in Havana, in the tomb of the Academia de Ciencias, to the right of [[André Voisin]].<ref>[https://www.miamiherald.com/news/local/community/miami-dade/article2159522.html Miami Herald: September 19, 2014: Lincoln Diaz-Balart tells own story, help needed to prevent suicide].</ref>

At the time of his death, he still held his positions with the Cuban Academy of Sciences and the Council of State.<ref name="Reuters-S"/>
